reply_text:
Kimi-2 has the gap data; the R-node bidding run has already finished. Two nodes failed outright and a few priming citations didn't pass the checker, so I'm looking at those.R13 and R15 hit "model at capacity", so I'm rerunning them:All 23 nodes are in. Writing the collation now.㊥ (Minard gap panel) The token data is being extended to today, and the hatched "no token data" region will go. The forensic report has no committed script behind it: codex-15 ran it by hand, which is why it stops at 21 September. kimi-2 is now writing `operator_gaps.py`, which rebuilds the gap and token table from the evidence store and the Codex session logs. Its acceptance test must reproduce the 09-21 report's own gaps, boundaries and token totals, with every mismatch listed and explained. Once that passes, I'll point the figure at the new data, remove the hatched region, re-check in the browser, publish and tell you.

㊢ (R-node bidding, finished) The run finished sooner than expected. All 23 nodes reported; R13 and R15 hit "model at capacity" and went through on rerun. The headline result:

| | Patterns | Hits |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bid on | 17 of 150 | 160 |
| Not bid on | 133 | 1,168 |

The 77 bids also bunch up:
- `war-machine/operational-not-decorative` drew 14 nodes;
- `workshop/records-carry-warrant` drew 11;
- `contracts/declare-the-reductions` drew 8.

These patterns are about how the code is built: typed refusals, recorded warrants, declared reductions. They don't say which AIF step the code performs. The more specific bids are few:
- `orchestration/recorded-handoff` (66 hits), bid by R9 through `check-independence` and by R10 through the scheduled dispatch ledger;
- `futon-theory/stop-the-line`, bid by R8, R6, R11 and R20, each through its own refusal or halt.

R3 (belief update) bid on nothing.

㊬ (what I checked) I opened three cited declarations and they are what the bids say:
- `admitFrom` in `PrefixFreeEnergyAtMachine.lean`, which stops at the first refusal;
- `check-independence` in `r9_checker.clj`;
- `halt!` in `tripwire.clj`.

The checker confirmed every bid's citation (file, line, symbol) and pattern id. Some priming claims cite catalogue rows loosely, and one R3a priming line points inside a function body. Those affect only the priming notes, not the bids.

🈖 (what this says about patterns to R-nodes) The library's functional patterns mostly describe engineering and coordination practice. The R-node code mostly implements AIF mathematics. Where the two meet is engineering practice, which every node shares. So reading R-nodes off the code gives almost no one-to-one alignment: 4 patterns have a single bidder and 13 are contested. Where a pattern is bid on, though, the link is specific and checkable, so the Arxana annotation half of your idea does work. Two options for getting turns onto R-nodes:
- **Bid on turns instead:** each node bids on operator turns rather than library patterns.
- **Topic patterns:** use the subject patterns that are about each node, which this round excluded.

Committed as futon0 `1b463aa`; the collation is in `rnode-bids/BIDS-collated-2026-10-01.md`.

㊢ (still running) kimi-1 has the in-place band decomposition and kimi-2 the gap data, each with a park on its job.

previous_reply_acts.text: (decomposing the band itself) Understood, and I've sent kimi-1 a corrected spec; it's working on it now. When you click a stage, the band in the main figure will split in place into its family stripes, filling exactly the band's own outline day by day. The panel below goes away. That should work out exactly, because each day's family averages add up to the stage's average, which a test already checks.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the rest of the spec) While a stage is open:
- **Legend:** the right-hand column shows that stage's families with their hits, under a header like "ASSURANCE BY FAMILY", in place of the count integral. The count integral comes back when you close it.
- **Hover:** a stripe gives stage, family, date and exact hits.
- **Closing:** clicking the band again, Escape, or "All stages" restores the plain band. Clicking another stage switches to it.
